title: The 2-Minute Gateway Step
explanation: Starting is often the hardest friction point. Reducing the opening commitment to a frictionless physical gesture lowers the barrier to entry.
suggested_action: Open the file or textbook, write only the date and title, and allow yourself to stop after 120 seconds if you still do not wish to continue.
safety_note: Never force a marathon session when task initiation is the primary obstacle.

title: Permitted Imperfect Draft
explanation: Separating content creation from critical evaluation silences the inner editor and allows early momentum.
suggested_action: Write three bullet points or a messy, unformatted paragraph that no one else will see. Treat this as disposable exploratory material.
safety_note: A rough draft is an active step forward, not a reflection of your intelligence or capability.

title: Decision De-escalation
explanation: When facing multiple competing priorities, choosing which task to do drains mental energy before work even begins.
suggested_action: Pick the item with the earliest deadline. Temporarily hide or cover all other tasks from your field of view for the next 25 minutes.
safety_note: Choosing one task does not mean abandoning the others; it protects your current attention.

title: The Sideways Entry
explanation: When the front door of a problem is locked, entering through an adjacent low-stress sub-part creates fresh perspective.
suggested_action: Instead of tackling the main argument or problem equation, format your bibliography, rename the variables, or sketch a diagram on scratch paper.
safety_note: Any forward movement within the subject domain creates cognitive familiarity.

title: Gentle Maintenance Mode
explanation: Pushing through acute exhaustion generates compounding frustration and negative association with the subject matter.
suggested_action: Switch to passive review: listen to an explanatory clip, skim headings, or rest with eyes closed for 15 minutes without guilt.
safety_note: Rest is an active cognitive maintenance phase, not lost or wasted time.

title: Perceptual Horizon Clear
explanation: Visual clutter and open digital tabs constantly trigger micro-attentional shifts, fragmenting working memory.
suggested_action: Close or minimize all browser tabs except the single active document. Put your phone out of arm's reach or in another room.
safety_note: Environmental nudges succeed where raw willpower fatigues.

title: The Bounded Container
explanation: An open-ended task feels like an infinite burden. A firm, short boundary makes the commitment psychologically manageable.
suggested_action: Set a timer for exactly 7 minutes. Commit only to staying with the document until the timer sounds.
safety_note: You have full agency to stop when the timer finishes.

title: Compassionate Horizon Re-entry
explanation: Dwelling on a missed deadline triggers shame and avoidance, delaying the resumption of productive work.
suggested_action: Acknowledge the current reality without self-blame. Recalculate your timeline based on where things stand right now today.
safety_note: The clock cannot be reversed, but the next hour is entirely within your control.

title: Sensory Reset & Grounding
explanation: Extended screen time locks eye accommodation and sympathetic nervous arousal, resulting in cognitive tunnel vision.
suggested_action: Look out a window at the furthest tree or horizon line for 60 seconds. Drink a glass of cold water and stretch your shoulders.
safety_note: Physical state shifts immediately relieve mental saturation.

title: Out-Loud Formulation
explanation: Translating internal confusion into spoken language engages the auditory processing cortex and clarifies logical gaps.
suggested_action: Explain out loud in plain words to an imaginary friend or object what you are trying to solve and where the logic breaks.
safety_note: You do not need to sound formal or academic when explaining the obstacle.

title: Interruption Resumption Anchor
explanation: Resuming work after an interruption fails when working memory has purged the immediate next thought.
suggested_action: Before stepping away or after resuming, write down the single next sentence or calculation you intended to produce.
safety_note: A tiny resumption anchor eliminates context-switching friction.

title: Scope De-Scoping
explanation: Projects bloat when nice-to-have secondary features are treated as mandatory prerequisites.
suggested_action: Identify the minimum viable submission or result that satisfies the core requirement and prune the rest for now.
safety_note: A finished core assignment is always more valuable than an incomplete masterpiece.
